# LCWIP selection
A random selection of 10 LCWIPs was made from the 2026 re-run of the LCWIP evidence collection process. 

```{r}
#| echo: true

# select 10 random numbers between and including 1 and 117
sample(1:117, 10)

```

**LCWIP IDs for review: **
7, 14, 26, 56, 57, 62, 80, 102, 106, 111

# LCWIP review
## Dover

- Title: Local Cycling & Walking Infrastructure Plan (LCWIP) for Dover District
- Author: Sustrans
- Date: December 2024
- PDF number: 7
- _idx: 44

**Notes**

- *how pct was used*: summarises well how PCT was used in LCWIP methodology
- *pct data sources*: commuting and school travel
    - **ERROR** -- also identifies desire lines as scenario
- *desire lines used*: true
    - **ERROR** -- PCT desire lines were not used in the LCWIP methodology, but the LCWIP does include desire lines for walking and cycling routes.
- *priorisation integration*: true
    - **ERROR** -- LCWIP does deal with prioritisation of routes, but it is not clear how the PCT data was integrated into this process.
- *length of cycle network proposed*: summarises well that total length not provided
- *total cost of network*: summarises well that total cost not provided
    - **NOTE** -- review of priorisation matrix (p67) shows cost for "easy wins" is £11.5m
- *specific evidence of impact of using pct*: summarises well how PCT shows cycling increases for different regions in different scenarios
    - **ERROR** -- review of LCWIP does not support claim result that "evidence directly shaped understanding of potential demand and justification for proposed network"

## Carlisle

- Title: Carlisle Local Cycling and Walking Infrastructure Plan (LCWIP) 2022-2037
- Author: Cumbria County Council
- Date: March 2022
- PDF number: 57
- _idx: 11

**Notes**
- *how pct was used*: 
    - **ERROR** -- the report only mentions PCT as being used to identify that most popular routs for both school and commuting are within the Carlisle urban area with specific mentions of certain routes. Unclear whether PCT was used in the LCWIP methodology itself.
- *specific evidence of impact*:
    - **ERROR** -- the report is unclear on PCT's impact on the methodology. Therefore, it is unclear to what extent the proposed priorisation cycling network is based on PCT data, if at all.
- *quotes on using pct*:
    - **ERROR** -- the quote captured does not appear in the LCWIP report. Possible hallucination of the AI model. The report does not provide any specific quotes on using PCT other than as a reference.

## Hart

- Title: Hart District Local Cycling and Walking Infrastructure Plan
- Author: Hampshire County Council
- Date: July 2024 (AI model says May 2023)
- PDF number: 80
- _idx: 23

**Notes**

- *how pct was used*: summarises well how PCT was used in LCWIP methodology
- *pct scenarios used*: Government Target, Go Dutch, E-bike
    - **ERROR** -- misses that baseline was also used
- *pct data sources*: commuting and school travel
    - **ERROR** -- also identifies desire lines as scenario
- *desire lines used": true
    - **ERROR** -- PCT desire lines were not used in the LCWIP methodology, but the LCWIP does include desire lines for walking and cycling routes.
    - **NOTE** -- the LCWIP does use the *Route Network* and *Fast Routes* outputs from PCT to inform the proposed cycling network and prioritisation.
- *specific evidence of impact*: summarises well how PCT had impact on the LCWIP methodology. The impact itself was that it directly informed the proposed cycling network routes and priorisation.
- *length of cycle network proposed*: plan does provide details of primary and secondary routes as part of proposed network. All proposed routes will not be ultimately developed as they are subject to a prioritisation process.
    - **NOTE** -- in the route audit it does provide distances for 12 primary cycle routes (total length 55km)
- *routes*: correctly identifies the aforementioned 12 primary cycle routes
